tasks.title: Add structured list filters to notes: project, type, since, until
tasks.description: Epic E-08. In packages/lane-memory (notes routes + notes-service): support query params project, type, since, until on the client-scoped notes list surface — either as filters on the existing list route or a dedicated filtered list route, implementer's call (decide-and-log in the PR body). Semantics: project and type match frontmatter fields exactly (case-insensitive); since/until are ISO-8601 timestamps filtered on updated_at, inclusive of since, exclusive of until; omitted params mean no constraint; unknown params are ignored, not errors. Auth stays client-scoped exactly as today — a client must never see another client's notes. Results ordered by updated_at descending. DO NOT remove, rename, or change the behaviour of semantic GET /v1/notes/search — this is purely additive. Do not add pagination in this task unless the existing list route already has it. Add or extend unit tests in packages/lane-memory covering: filter by project, filter by type, since/until boundary, and combined filters. Prefer extracting a pure predicate/query-builder helper so tests do not require live Postgres.

tasks.title: Portfolio registry — one file listing every project the hub watches
tasks.description: Epic E-09, foundation for T-0051..T-0053. Create docs/personal-steward/portfolio-registry.json: a founder-owned, version-controlled list of the projects the hub collects from. Deliberately a repo file, NOT a database table — the founder edits it, it needs no migration, and it is readable by an agent from GitHub without credentials. Each entry: slug (lowercase, stable, the key everything else joins on), display_name, github (owner/repo), github_default_branch, zeabur_project_name (or null if not deployed there), runtime_report_url (null for now — see E-10), expected_cadence_hours (how often a report should appear; used for staleness detection in T-0053), enabled (bool), notes. Also write a short docs/personal-steward/portfolio-collectors.md explaining the three lines (autopilot / deploy / runtime), that git commit sha is the correlation key across them, and how to add a project. Docs only — no code, no schema change. Keep it small; this is the thing a future session reads first.

tasks.title: Git collector — read each project's autopilot state from GitHub
tasks.description: Epic E-09, report line 1 (autopilot). Add a collector that, for each enabled project in portfolio-registry.json, reads these files from the project's default branch via the GitHub API: docs/autopilot/backlog.json, roadmap.json, locks.json, pause-state.json, and docs/autopilot/reports/latest.json IF present. Also read recent commits on the default branch for the period. Normalise into the hub report shape (ai-dev-methodologies portfolio-hub-reporting.md, edge='repo', schema_version '1.1') and store as a note in the personal-jacky client with frontmatter type='report', project=<slug>, edge='repo', period={since,until}, and a source_sha field carrying the head commit read. IMPORTANT — do NOT require the project to generate anything: the raw autopilot state is already committed by Maker/Checker on every run, so the collector derives the report itself. This is what makes onboarding a project a registry row rather than a task in that repo. Derive: shipped = commits/PR titles merged in the period (extract T-xxxx ids where present); autopilot = counts by task status + whether pause-state is set + any held locks; needs_founder = tasks in needs_human plus open decisions.json entries; risks = tasks with retries>0 and ready tasks untouched for a long time; intent_vs_actual = previous period's ask vs what shipped, or 'none' on first run; ask = at most one. GitHub credential: read-only token, resolved through packages/lane-credentials (three of the five repos are PRIVATE — powerhouse, ai-business, ViOS — so an unauthenticated read will silently return nothing for them; treat a 404 on a registered private repo as a FAILURE to surface, never as an empty report). Prefer a pure normalise function taking already-fetched file contents so tests need no network. Wire as a scheduled job using the existing packages/lane-harness pattern — read how AT1b harnesses are registered before inventing a new scheduling mechanism. Do NOT write to any project repo; this collector is read-only toward products.

tasks.title: Zeabur collector — deployment status per project
tasks.description: Epic E-09, report line 2 (deploy). This closes a real blind spot: today a merge marks a task done, but if the Zeabur build fails the code never reaches production, and the Checker's WATCHDOG can still PASS because it curls a URL that is happily serving the PREVIOUS successful deployment. STEP 1 — SCHEMA FIRST, DO NOT GUESS FIELD NAMES. Zeabur's public docs (https://zeabur.com/docs/en-US/developer/public-api) document projects(ownerID), buildLogs(projectID, deploymentID, timestampCursor) and runtimeLogs(...), but do NOT document the query that LISTS deployments and their statuses — it exists (buildLogs requires a deploymentID) but only appears in the full schema. Fetch the SDL from the Apollo Explorer at https://api.zeabur.com/apollo-explorer (login required) or introspect the endpoint with the API key, find the deployment listing query, and RECORD the exact query you used in docs/personal-steward/portfolio-collectors.md so the next session does not repeat this discovery. If introspection is disabled and the schema cannot be obtained, STOP and mark needs_human with what you tried — do not brute-force field names. STEP 2 — endpoint https://api.zeabur.com/graphql, header 'Authorization: Bearer <key>', key from Dashboard > Settings > API Keys, stored in packages/lane-credentials, NEVER in source or logs. Note the key is tied to a personal account and may need ownerID for team-owned projects. STEP 3 — for each registered project with a zeabur_project_name, collect the most recent deployments in the period: id, status, the git commit sha it built, started/finished timestamps, and the service/environment. THE COMMIT SHA IS THE POINT — it is what joins this line to the git line, letting the hub say 'T-0002 merged as abc123 but its deployment failed'. If Zeabur does not expose the sha on a deployment, say so explicitly in the PR body and fall back to timestamp correlation, marked in the report as lower confidence. Store as a note: type='report', project=<slug>, edge='deploy'. Use the same six-section shape; put failed builds under risks and, when a failure blocks shipped work, under needs_founder. Only fetch build LOGS for failed deployments — logs are large and mostly noise when green. Reuse the lane-harness scheduling pattern. Read-only: never trigger, redeploy, or roll back from the collector.

tasks.title: Portfolio brief tool + staleness detection over MCP
tasks.description: Epic E-09, the surface a Claude session actually calls. Add an MCP tool (packages/lane-mcp, alongside the existing note tools) named portfolio_brief that returns, for a requested period and optional project filter, the collected reports across all registered projects joined per project. STALENESS IS A FIRST-CLASS FINDING, NOT AN ERROR: for every enabled project in the registry, compare the newest collected report against expected_cadence_hours; if none arrived in time, emit an explicit stale entry saying which line is missing and how long it has been silent. This is the single most valuable thing the hub does that no project can do for itself — a project whose collector silently died looks 'fine' to anyone reading its last report, and only the hub knows a report was due and never came. Never omit a registered project from the output just because it has no data; absence must be visible. Also join the lines by commit sha where available so the tool can report chains like 'T-0002 → sha abc123 → deployment failed', and flag any sha that merged but has no successful deployment. Mark each field's provenance so a reading agent never relays a guess as a fact: measured (read from an API), derived (computed from measured data), or asserted (text a project wrote about itself). Return structured JSON, not prose — the calling agent writes the prose. Do NOT pre-filter by importance: send everything for the period and let the calling agent triage, because what matters is often only visible across projects. Auth stays client-scoped like the other MCP tools. Add tests with fixture reports covering: a healthy project, a stale project, and a project whose merge has no successful deploy.
